clue.text: This could well be a strain for the skilled worker

indicators.note: the clue suggests these letters might well form something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A craftsman's job is a constant strain on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could well be' tells you to rearrange A STRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman trained in a manual trade is a skilled worker.

clue.text: About to enter a plea for approval

indicators.note: the abbreviation for about goes into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: a plea is a claim made in argument
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone files a plea hoping it will be approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts C inside A CLAIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud public praise and approval are synonyms.

clue.text: Yielding, reverse vehicle on board

indicators.note: the word for the vehicle is to be read backwards

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle
a table is a board, as in 'bed and board'

explanation.surface: A driver backs a vehicle up on to a ferry deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' turns CART into TRAC, which sits above TABLE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something yielding is easily managed or docile, a synonym.

clue.text: The fight to get started

explanation.surface: A boxing match is about to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief fight or squabble; also, as two words, the phrasal verb meaning begin work vigorously.

clue.text: Fine point put on a pointer.

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass
an arrow is a pointer on a sign

explanation.surface: A sharp tip is fixed on to a dart or pointer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' in a down clue sets N above ARROW.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine and slender mean the same, as in a fine margin.

clue.text: This miser is a fool accepting credit with little hesitation

indicators.note: the word for a fool takes in the credit abbreviation

parts.note: a sap is a fool
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
er is a brief hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A stingy person is foolish to take on credit without thinking twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts CR inside SAP, then ER follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser scrapes together every penny, so a penny-pincher is a scraper.

clue.text: The condemnation of "X' in dreadful scene

indicators.note: the number goes inside the rearranged letters
dreadful signals the letters of scene are mangled

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A dreadful scene in which someone marked X is condemned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' turns SCENE into SENCE, and 'in' puts TEN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's pronouncement of punishment is a condemnation.

clue.text: Check leisure includes exercise

indicators.note: the word for leisure holds the word for exercise inside it

parts.note: rest is leisure
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Leisure time with some workout included should be kept in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts TRAIN inside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-control or curb is a check on behaviour.

clue.text: Quiet with an associate, but quite friendly

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
an ally is an associate

explanation.surface: Someone who's quiet with a colleague but rather friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on chummy terms means being friendly.

clue.text: Chafes about a minister's obscure statements

indicators.note: the word for chafes goes round the minister's letters

parts.note: riles means irritates or chafes
DD, doctor of divinity, is a minister; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A clergyman's vague sermon irritates the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts DD round inside RILES: RI-DD-LES.
explanation.definitionFit: Puzzling sayings or enigmas are obscure statements.

clue.text: Figure the second will create a disturbance

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral figure for a hundred
the latter is the second of two

explanation.surface: Picking the second figure will cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a loud rattling racket is to create a disturbance.

clue.text: Got comfortable home and got ahead

parts.note: a nest is a home
led means was in front, got ahead

explanation.surface: Someone settled into their house and moved up in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Snuggled down cosily means got comfortable.

clue.text: Holder of Her Majesty's star appointment?

definitions.text: Holder of Her Majesty's star appointment?

parts.words: Holder of Her Majesty's star appointment
parts.note: a top royal post read literally as the royal post about the stars

explanation.surface: Who holds the Queen's most prestigious post?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star appointment' looks like a top job, but read literally it is a post concerned with stars: the honorary British royal astronomer.
explanation.definitionFit: The title given to the senior royal astronomer in Britain, a royal appointment concerning stars.

clue.text: A port in Alabama that's changing rapidly

explanation.surface: An Alabama harbour town is in rapid flux.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf coast city in Alabama; also, the adjective for something moving or changing freely.

clue.text: A hold-up for the viewers' benefit

definitions.text: A hold-up for the viewers' benefit

parts.words: A hold-up for the viewers' benefit
parts.note: not a robbery but spectacles on a handle, held up to the eyes

explanation.surface: A robbery staged so that onlookers can watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold-up' suggests a robbery; the viewers are eyes, and the object is spectacles held up on a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeglasses on a long handle, held up to the eyes, help the viewers see.

clue.text: Greek fighter of some eminence among experts

indicators.note: the eminence goes inside the word for experts

parts.note: aces are experts
a hill is an eminence, a piece of high ground

explanation.surface: A Greek warrior of some distinction among the experts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts HILL inside ACES; 'eminence' looks like fame but is a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: The great warrior of Homer's Iliad was a Greek fighter.

clue.text: This criminal's alternative isn't clear

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of the letters is called for

explanation.surface: A crook claims his alibi isn't clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' tells you to rearrange ISNT CLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who commits larceny is a criminal.

clue.text: Artist expressing admiration for an attractive girl?

definitions.text: expressing admiration for an attractive girl

explanation.surface: A painter wolf-whistles at a pretty woman.
explanation.definitionFit: James McNeill Whistler was an American painter; also, someone who gives a wolf-whistle of admiration.

clue.text: Divine directors, though they may appear round the bend!

indicators.note: the pronoun's letters surround the bend

parts.note: taken as written
an arch is a bend or curve

explanation.surface: Heavenly rulers might seem quite mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round the bend' looks like 'mad', but 'round' puts ARCH inside THEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule by gods, or a body of divine rulers, is a set of divine directors.

clue.text: Split over low turnover in a catering establishment

parts.note: to tear is to split

indicators.note: the cow's sound is turned over, read upwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound of cattle

explanation.surface: A row over falling turnover at a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' sets TEAR on top in the down entry; 'turnover' reverses MOO to OOM. 'Low' is the cow's call, not 'down'.
explanation.definitionFit: A place serving light refreshments is a catering establishment.

clue.text: The way metal containers are displayed in shops

parts.note: St, street, is a way
ores are rocks that contain metal

explanation.surface: How metal tins are laid out in shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Large retail outlets are shops.

clue.text: The fellow spending his days backing horses

definitions.text: The fellow spending his days backing horses

parts.words: The fellow spending his days backing horses
parts.note: not a gambler but a craftsman whose goods go on horses' backs

explanation.surface: A man who spends his days betting on racehorses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing horses' suggests betting; here it is making the leather seats that go on a horse's back.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker of saddles provides what horses carry on their backs.

clue.text: Shipping airmen out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of airmen are scattered

explanation.surface: Air force personnel are being shipped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' asks you to rearrange AIRMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine means relating to the sea and shipping.

clue.text: There's a Canadian all for making a profession of faith

indicators.note: making signals building something new from these letters

explanation.surface: A Canadian is keen to declare his religious beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' tells you to rearrange THERES A CANADIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christian creed attributed to Athanasius is a formal statement of belief.

clue.text: Vagrants book into house — very large

indicators.note: the book abbreviation goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: OS, outsize, means very large

explanation.surface: Tramps take a book into a huge house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts B between HO and OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramps or homeless wanderers are vagrants.

clue.text: Feature a far-away land

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A news feature about a distant country.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Asian country is a distant land from Britain.

clue.text: Going round is spoken about very little

indicators.note: the word for spoken goes about the small amount

parts.note: oral means spoken
a bit is a very little

explanation.surface: Gossip that little is being said about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts BIT inside ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Circling in an orbit means going round.

clue.text: Beginning in it, one joins a trainee

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A newcomer joins a trainee who is just starting out.
explanation.definitionFit: First or opening means beginning.

clue.text: The therapist Erasmus converted

indicators.note: converted means the letters are changed into another form

explanation.surface: The scholar Erasmus has a religious conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' tells you to rearrange ERASMUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives massages is a physical therapist.

clue.text: One-time player — such a demanding individual.

parts.note: ex means former, one-time
an actor is a player

explanation.surface: A former actor is now a very demanding person.
explanation.definitionFit: One who exacts or extorts is a demanding person.
